entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Francisco Plancarte y Navarrete was born in Zamora, Michoacán, Mexico, the son of Jesus Plancarte Labastida and Maria de los Angeles Navarrete. He had two younger sisters, Maria Gertrudis and Maria Benita Virginia. According to his baptismal certificate, dated October 27, 1856, he was called José Francisco Hilarión. He grew up in a very religious family, and at the age of thirteen, support by his uncle, Antonio Plancarte y Labastida, he entered the Pontifical Latin American College in Rome. During the thirteen years that he lived in Europe doing his ecclesiastical studies, he visited museums, ruins and ancient monuments, and he observed archeological digs.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Mexican clergyman who studied in Rome and witnessed archaeological excavations firsthand, Francisco Plancarte y Navarrete's experiences likely influenced his understanding of Mesoamerican history and culture. His exposure to European art and architecture may have also shaped his own artistic pursuits.
